item.title: Pennsylvania allocates $37m for more than 500 new EV charging ports
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: The US state of Pennsylvania has announced a multimillion dollar investment in public EV charging infrastructure. This will fund 515 new charging ports across five counties as part of the federal NEVI programme.

item.title: Believ takes over 110+ EV chargers in Brighton & Hove
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: UK charge point operator Believ has taken over more than 110 public EV chargers across 30 locations in the English city of Brighton & Hove. The chargers were previously operated by Blink Charging.

item.title: OEMs may have to take back EVs with faulty batteries
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: EU product safety law could provide buyers of electric cars with potentially defective high-voltage batteries an additional way to return their vehicles. The Offenburg Regional Court explicitly allows the reversal of the purchase in a case involving a Cupra Born based on the EU Product Safety Regulation.

item.title: Volkswagen pauses development of the ID.Golf
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Volkswagen is temporarily pausing development work on the future ID.Golf. The automaker cites high cost pressure as the reason for the decision and plans to resume work as soon as the necessary investments can be secured.

item.title: E.ON acquires Smatrics EnBW Italia
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: After a two-year interlude, Smatrics EnBW is once again withdrawing from Italy and selling its four charging parks in the north of the country, to E.ON. The sites house a total of 64 fast-charging points. The purchase price is undisclosed.

item.title: Miele orders 840 electric transporters from Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Miele plans to expand its European service fleet with 840 battery-electric transporters from Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles. 440 vehicles are set to be deployed in Germany.

item.title: Allye introduces 400 kW fast charger with second-life batteries
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: British company Allye Energy has unveiled the MEV, a battery-buffered fast charger for depots. The system uses complete second-life batteries from EVs and is designed to provide up to 400 kW of charging power without necessarily requiring a more powerful grid connection.

item.title: Group14 to build battery material factory in Sagunt
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: US battery material manufacturer Group14, which specializes in silicon anodes, will in future also produce in Europe. The commitment to establish a production site in Spain is directly linked to a new capital increase - specifically, with a European investor.

item.title: Vingroup to build a €449-million EV plant in the Philippines
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: In an effort to strengthen its footprint in the Southeast Asian auto market, Vingroup - the parent company of VinFast plans to build a new EV manufacturing facility in the Philippines. The Vietnamese conglomerate will invest US$500 million (approx. €449 million euros) in the new site.

item.title: Nio Firefly receives battery upgrade in China – with swap option for existing customers
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Nio is granting the Firefly in China another upgrade. While the power output was increased in spring 2026, the focus is now on the battery and, consequently, the range. The manufacturer has announced an option for a 60 kWh battery. This battery has the same dimensions as the 42 kWh battery, meaning existing customers can also opt for a battery swap.

item.title: Rivian boosts revenue thanks to R2 and VW partnership
item.dc:creator: Florian Treiss
item.description: Rivian's revenue grew by 38 per cent in the third quarter of 2026 to $2.16 billion. Both the EV manufacturer's deliveries and its software and services business saw significant growth. 16 per cent of the revenue alone came from the partnership with Volkswagen. Rivian has also raised its annual forecast.

item.title: BYD plots new battery-electric coach launch in UK
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: BYD is set to battery-electric coach in the UK market by the end of the year, according to Frank Thorpe, BYD's Managing Director for Commercial Vehicle UK. The model is said to be specifically developed for the UK market.

item.title: Ireland connects EV fleet depots to electricity flexibility markets
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: An Post and DHL Express Ireland are taking part in a new project that connects EV fleet depots directly to Ireland's electricity flexibility markets, allowing operators to adjust charging demand in response to grid conditions - and potentially generate new revenue.

item.title: The BMW iX3 50 xDrive: is the Neue Klasse a breakthrough?
item.dc:creator: Peter Schwierz
item.description: BMW is entering a new era with the iX3. The first production model of the Neue Klasse aims to impress with high efficiency, enormous range, new software, and bidirectional charging. But how well does the overall package work in everyday life? We tested the BMW iX3 50 xDrive for two weeks on highways, country roads, in city traffic, and as a mobile power storage unit – and encountered some surprises along the way.

item.title: UK government pledges £100m to cut public EV charging costs
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: The funding, which was included in the 2026 Autumn Budget, aims to lower charging prices for drivers who use 'local, lower-powered' chargers such as those installed on lampposts or pavements. The money will be distributed over the course of two years, starting from spring 2027.

item.title: Hyundai reveals UK pricing for new Ioniq 6
item.dc:creator: Ciaran Daly
item.description: The Ioniq 6 has received a facelift, and with it, new UK pricing. Hyundai's updated electric saloon is now available to order from a starting price of £33,240. Deliveries are planned for early 2027.

item.title: Volta Via examines electrification of road construction sites
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: The Volta Via research project has investigated how large construction sites in road building can be electrified and what energy infrastructure is required. Electrified models are already available for up to 86 per cent of the machine classes considered.

item.title: Portugal considers 80 per cent EV purchase subsidies
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: Portugal will support low-income households in purchasing an electric car with up to 80 per cent of the vehicle price in the future. The new program is expected to cover around 20,000 vehicles. In parallel, the government will continue its regular electric car incentive program with a budget of €50 million euros.

item.title: CATL advances solid-state battery development to 20 Ah samples
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: According to Chinese media, CATL has expanded the development of its solid-state battery from a 10-Ah-class validation platform to test runs with 20-Ah samples. The company continues to aim for small-scale production in 2027 and is reportedly targeting an energy density of around 500 Wh/kg.

item.title: Vehicle recycling at VW: dismantling line opens in Zwickau
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Volkswagen has opened its dismantling line at the Zwickau plant. From 2027, the new facility is expected to disassemble and recycle around 4,100 vehicles annually. Across the entire 'circular economy' business hub at the Zwickau site, an initial 100 jobs could eventually grow into 1,000 new positions.

item.title: VW unveils global plans for new tech package developed in China
item.dc:creator: Victoria Zippmann
item.description: Volkswagen Group China has presented a new technology package and plans for marketing it outside China. In future, the company aims to use its local developments for global markets - and expand its China location into a central innovation and export hub.

item.title: India: Ampstar bags order for 100 electric heavy-duty trucks
item.dc:creator: Sagar Parikh
item.description: Ampstar, the new electric commercial vehicle brand from Indian conglomerate JSW Group's JSW Greentech subsidiary, has secured its first commercial order, comprising 100 electric heavy-duty trucks. It will supply these trucks to JSW Cement, another JSW Group subsidiary.

item.title: Ford Model e division reports sustained losses in Q3
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Ford has released its financial results for the third quarter of 2026. For the US automaker, all-electric passenger cars remain a massive loss-making business, with the Model e division accumulating US$1.1 billion in losses between July and September. However, this is a lower figure than in the same quarter last year.

item.title: ATM orders 110 electric buses from Karsan amid Italian e-bus boom
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: Turkish manufacturer Karsan has secured a tender by Milan's public transport company ATM for the delivery of 110 electric buses. The vehicles, of the Karsan e-ATA 12 model, are set to enter service gradually starting from the end of 2027.

item.title: Alternative truck drivetrains: Why Ihro is now fully committed to electric trucks
item.dc:creator: Nicole de Jong
item.description: Logistics company Ihro is currently integrating 15 MAN eTGX trucks into its fleet of around 200 vehicles. The mid-sized company from the Hohenlohe district is known for its experimental approach, having tested its first electric special-purpose vehicle as early as 2016, and remains undeterred by recent setbacks with gas-powered trucks.

item.title: Battery-electric trucks gain ground in key markets; electric buses near-ubiquitous
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: The latest ACEA figures show that European commercial vehicle markets are growing, amid disproportionate demand for electric trucks and buses. In the first nine months of the year, electric trucks saw a 50 per cent sales increase, while electric buses rose by 38 per cent. However, the starting level for electric trucks remains modest, whereas electric buses are now almost standard in orders.

item.title: Fuuse and Drax to migrate 14,000 BP Pulse fleet charging sockets
item.dc:creator: Nicole Storch
item.description: Fuuse and Drax Electric Vehicles will support almost 1,000 fleet customers as BP Pulse exits workplace charging. The partnership aims to keep existing chargers operational, preserve hardware warranties and avoid costly replacements.

item.title: Florida campus police deploy manned eVTOLs
item.dc:creator: Cora Werwitzke
item.description: The Florida Polytechnic University Police Department is the first law enforcement agency in the USA to integrate a manned electric aircraft into its operational service. The vertical take-off aircraft is "in the final phase of the approval process," according to the university.

item.title: London Ambulance Service secures charging partners
item.dc:creator: guest author
item.description: London Ambulance Service (LAS) has contracted providers to ensure its expanding fleet of electric vehicles can be charged when and where they need power across the UK capital. SEE Services will install and maintain charging facilities and has appointed Optimo Energy as its Fleet Energy Operating System partner.

item.title: AMG Lithium opens test laboratory for solid electrolytes in Frankfurt
item.dc:creator: Jasmin Apitzsch-Krause
item.description: AMG Lithium has commissioned its new Performance Lab "PerLa" in Frankfurt, Germany. The company aims to test sulfide solid electrolytes under more realistic conditions in complete laboratory cells and further develop them with customers.
